intent: A record held by a ghost: the gold bars put Hungary's 3 above Brazil's 2 and Argentina's 2, the unbeaten counter climbs to 42 matches, and a pin lands on the Budapest stadium where the golden team played.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Who has the MOST Olympic golds in men's football?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Who has the most Olympic golds in men's football?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Hungary. 3 golds, the last of them in 1968.

lines.direction: ease back so the whole country sits in frame; the gold bars rise on 'Brazil' with the Brazilian flag-ball thinking; the Argentine flag-ball thinks on 'Argentina'; a gold medal sticker on 'Hungary' as the country pulses
lines.text: Brazil has 2, Argentina has 2. Great Britain also has 3, but Hungary's came last, so Hungary holds the record.

lines.direction: pull right out so Hungary and Finland share the frame; a sparkle on 'Magical'; on 'Helsinki' a yellow line draws from Budapest north to Helsinki with a football sticker travelling along it; the 42-unbeaten card and a medal on 'defeat' as Hungary pulses
lines.text: The golden team were the Magical Magyars. They travelled from Budapest to Helsinki in 1952 and went 42 matches without defeat.

lines.direction: push in on the capital; the stadium pin and tag land on 'Budapest' with a stadium sticker; the SINCE 1972 card on 'qualified'; the Hungarian flag-ball shrugs happy on 'years' with a ghost sticker as the country pulses; pin leaves
lines.text: Their home was the Nepstadion in Budapest. Hungary has not qualified for the Olympics for more than 50 years.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A record nobody has touched. Follow us.
